page: Microsoft Azure D4lds_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine belonging to the Dldsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 6973P-C cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and is equipped with a 480 MB L3 cache. System memory is constrained to 8.0 GB, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. The instance includes 236 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage, but does not bundle any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-threaded capabilities, with gzip compression reaching 36.23 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.92 GB/sec. However, multi-threaded scaling is weaker, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 4655.9 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 29.51 GB/sec. Memory performance is mixed; while large block read-only bandwidth averages 43.66 GB/sec, write bandwidth and small-block cached read bandwidth are relatively weak. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions), which assist in workloads like lightweight AI inference, where it achieves 634.3 tokens/sec for 135M model prompt processing.

Given its low-memory configuration relative to the CPU core count, the D4lds_v7 offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-centric workloads that do not demand large memory footprints. The inclusion of 236 GB of local storage provides a resource-dense option for temporary data handling. This server is best suited for single-threaded tasks, lightweight web serving, basic database operations, and entry-level batch processing where high clock speed is prioritized over massive memory capacity.
